2. CASE OF THE PLAINTIFF AS PER PLAINT

The necessary facts for the adjudication of the present suit, as stated in the plaint, are as under :
2.1. That the plaintiffs are husband and wife and reputed members of the Society.

The plaintiff no.1 is a businessman and an income tax payee and during the Assessment Year 2019-2020, he had a gross total income of Rs.5,65,300/- and the plaintiff no.2 is Suresh Kumar And Anr vs Nageshwar Rai And Anr on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57716398/

The plaintiff no.2 was the owner and in possession of a freehold plot bearing no.121, admeasuring about 166 sq. yds, part of Khasra no.78/13/2, situated in the Revenue Estate of Village Nangloi Jat, Colony now known as Nihal Vihar in Block Tej Ram Park, Nangloi, New Delhi and in the year 2005, defendant no.1 approached the plaintiff no.1 and after negotiations they entered into an agreement for the sale of a portion of land admeasuring 42 sq.yds out of the aforesaid plot and in pursuance thereof on 17.03.2005, plaintiff no.2 transferred 42 sq.yds out of the aforesaid plot to defendant no.2 at the total sale consideration amount of Rs.10,00,000/- and thereafter the peaceful possession of the said land was handed over to the defendants.
2.3.

The defendants in collusion with each other made a false, concocted and malicious complaint against the plaintiffs dated 09.10.2015 alleging cheating and on the basis of which FIR bearing no.1180/2015 under Section 420/120-B IPC was registered at Police Station Nihal Vihar and the plaintiffs were constrained to file bail application seeking anticipatory bail dated 30.11.2015 and after several hearings, an order dated 31.03.2016 was made whereby anticipatory bail was granted to the plaintiffs and when their neighbours and associates learnt of the said complaint, it caused immense humiliation to them as such they were insulted and defamed by the said acts of the defendants.
2.4. After the completion of the investigation of the aforesaid FIR, the plaintiffs were chargesheeted under Section 420/120B/34 IPC and ultimately, the said criminal proceedings were terminated after the discharge order passed by the Ld.
Metropolitan Magistrate.
2.5. The plaintiffs have suffered due to the malicious prosecution initiated at the instance of the defendants and are entitled to recover Rs.10,00,000/- from the defendants as damages.
3. Summons of the suit were issued to the defendants and defendants put their appearance through counsel on 27.08.2020 and joint written statement was filed on their behalf.
4. CASE OF THE DEFENDANTS.
4.1. The defendants are husband and wife and the present suit instituted by plaintiffs is not maintainable as the averments raised therein are frivolous, contrary to law and without any legal basis.

13. ISSUE No.1:-
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to decree in the sum of Rs.10,00,000/-, as prayed for?
The onus to prove this issue is upon the plaintiffs.

Plaintiff no.1 Sh. Suresh Kumar stepped into the witness box as PW-1 and stated that he and his wife Smt. The plaintiff further deposed that almost after ten years of the aforesaid transaction, the defendants got lodged a false FIR against him and plaintiff no.2 under Section 420/120 IPC and after the registration of the FIR, he was constrained to move bail applications before the Ld. sentences.text: The plaintiff no.1 has further pleaded that owing to the false FIR which was got lodged at the instance of the defendants, the plaintiffs suffered a lot of physical and mental harassment as well as defamation and had to incur expenses during the aforesaid legal proceedings which caused them severe monetary losses.

13.2. The plaintiffs have also examined PW-2 Sh. Manoj and PW-3 Sh.Jaybir Singh for establishing the loss of reputation suffered by them due to the lodging of false FIR against them at the instance of defendants.

13.3. In rebuttal, the defendants have categorically denied the allegations of the plaintiffs and defendant no.2 / Smt. Dharamsheela Devi examined herself as a defence witness and deposed that she filed the criminal complaint against the plaintiffs as the entire original chain of property documents pertaining to the plot admeasuring 42 sq.yds were not handed over to them by the plaintiffs and due to which they had to face several difficulties and the criminal complaint was not filed with any malice or ulterior motive.
13.4. The crux of the case set up by the plaintiffs lies in the tort of malicious prosecution.
Malicious prosecution means "the institution of a criminal or civil proceedings for an improper purpose and without probable cause ".

sentences.text: 13.5. The Hon'ble High Court further observed that in a suit for malicious prosecution, the plaintiff must disclose in the plaint the ulterior reason or purpose for which the defendant prosecuted him.

13.6. During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for plaintiffs pleaded that the defendants are liable to pay the damages as the criminal proceedings initiated at their instance ultimately terminated in favour of plaintiffs.
13.7. This Court is of the opinion that there is no presumption in law of a prosecution ending in an acquittal being malicious.

So, a plaint in a suit for compensation for malicious prosecution merely stating that the plaintiff was prosecuted by or at the instance of the defendant and later on acquitted, would not constitute the valid cause of action.

In the present case, before getting into the appreciation of evidence for arriving at the finding as to whether the case set up by the plaintiffs satisfies the pre- requisites of a suit for malicious prosecution, this Court deems fit to note down some of the admitted facts of the present case which are not in dispute.
13.9.

Firstly, the plaintiffs were discharged in the criminal case which was instituted on the complaint of defendant no.2 / Smt. Dharamsheela Devi and in the discharge order Ex.PW-1/6, it has been specifically observed by the Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate that the charge against the accused persons (plaintiffs herein) for the offence punishable under Section 420/120B IPC is groundless.

The Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate also observed that there was nothing on record to indicate that the accused persons (plaintiffs herein) had dishonest intention at the time of the time of the execution of registered Sale Deed dated 17.03.2005.
13.10.Secondly, it is a matter of record that the plaintiffs executed the registered Sale Deed qua the property in question (plot of 42 sq.yds) in favour of defendant no.2 on 17.03.2005 and the criminal complaint on the basis of which the FIR Ex.PW-1/3 was got lodged, was filed on 09.10.2015.

The aforesaid fact reveals that the criminal case was initiated against the plaintiffs after more than ten years of the date on which the title and possession of the property in question was transferred to the defendants by the plaintiffs and no grievance was raised during the intervening period.
13.11.Thirdly, in his cross examination, defendant no.2 / Smt. Dharamsheela Devi has admitted that after the purchase of property in question, she got constructed two floors thereon and have taken electricity connections and further rented out the same to the tenants.
She has specifically admitted that she is earning rental income from the three floors which have been constructed upon the property in question purchased from the plaintiffs.

13.12.Fourthly, it is a matter of record that in the criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 and FIR Ex.PW-1/3, the defendant no.2 / Smt. Dharamsheela Devi levelled a serious allegation against the plaintiffs by alleging that the plot no.RZC-202, Khasra No.78/13/5, Nihal Vihar, out of which they purchased 42 sq.yds did not belong to the plaintiffs and they had cheated the defendants by transferring the property which actually did not belong to them.

However, in the written statement and her evidence affidavit Ex.DW-1/X, she has taken the stand that the criminal complaint against the plaintiffs was filed as she did not receive the original chain of documents pertaining to the aforesaid property.

Fifthly, the defendants have the possession of the registered Sale Deed dated 17.03.2005 vide which the plot admeasuring 42 sq.yds. was transferred in the favour of defendant no.2 at the instance of plaintiff no.2.
13.14.Now

, this Court will consider as to whether the case set up by the plaintiffs embodies the four requisites of malicious prosecution as discussed above. a. Initiation or continuation of a law suit :

sentences.text: The present suit has been filed seeking damages for malicious prosecution by the plaintiffs against the defendants for filing a criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 on the basis of which the FIR Ex.PW-1/3 was got lodged and the criminal investigation was initiated which ultimately culminated in filing the chargesheet before the Court against the plaintiffs.
So, the pre-condition of the initiation of a law suit stands satisfied.
b. Favourable termination of law suit.

The criminal prosecution against the plaintiffs which was initiated after the lodging of FIR Ex.PW-1/3 at the instance of defendants stood terminated after the passing of the discharge order Ex.PW-1/6 dated 04.09.2019 passed by Ld.Metropolitan Magistrate at the stage of charge framing.
So, the pre-condition of termination of law suit in favour of the plaintiff stands satisfied.
c. Lack of probable cause.

In Gangadhar Padhy Vs. Prem Singh, (2014) 211 DLT 104, it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that to show that there was no reasonable and probable cause, it has to be shown that the defendant did not believe in the plaintiff's guilt.

entities.text: Gangadhar Padhy Vs. Prem Singh, (2014) 211 DLT 104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the perusal of criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 filed on behalf of the defendants on the basis of which the FIR Ex.PW-1/3 was registered, it is crystal clear that the same was filed by taking the plea that the defendants have been cheated by the plaintiffs by transferring a piece of land which did not belong to them.

However, in her written statement and evidence affidavit Ex.DW-1/X, the defendant no.2 / Smt.
Dharamsheela Devi changed her version and deposed that the criminal case was filed against the plaintiffs as she did not receive the original chain of documents pertaining to the property in question, the aforesaid variation in the version of defendants reflects that even defendant no.2 did not believe in the allegations levelled by her against the plaintiffs in her criminal complaint regarding the offence of cheating allegedly committed by the plaintiffs.
So, the pre-condition of lack of probable cause also stands satisfied.
d. Malice.

At the very outset, it needs to be underlined that the plaintiffs have merely used the word ' malice' in the body of their plaint without elaborating regarding the ulterior reason or purpose for which they were prosecuted by the defendants.

However, this Court is of the opinion that even in the absence of any such elaboration if the element of malice is founded on the part of the defendants, from the appreciation of the evidence of the present case, the pre- condition of presence of malice for the prosecution of defendants for the tort of malicious prosecution would be satisfied.

sentences.text: Malicious prosecution is the institution of a criminal or civil proceedings for an improper purpose and without probable cause.

13.16.The present case seeking damages is founded upon the institution of the criminal case at the instance of defendants against the plaintiffs wherein the plaintiffs were finally discharged and the criminal proceedings came to an end, so it is relevant to compare the original criminal complaint filed by the defendants therein with the case set up by the defendants in the form of written statement and evidence affidavit in the present case.

It is a matter of record that in the criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 on the basis of which FIR Ex.PW-1/3 was lodged, the defendants levelled a very specific allegation against the plaintiffs by alleging that the plot in question did not belong to the plaintiffs at the relevant time and they had cheated the defendants by transferring the property which actually belonged to a third person, while in her evidence before this Court, defendant no.2 deposed that the criminal complaint was filed against the plaintiffs as they did not handover the original chain of documents of the plot in question to her and due to which they were facing several problems.

This Court is of the opinion that the aforesaid narration of facts reveals that the ulterior reason behind filing the said complaint Ex.PW-1/2 was not due to any deception practiced by the plaintiffs upon the defendants and resultant unlawful loss rather the said police complaint was filed due to non-handing over of the previous chain of the property documents of the plot in question, in original.
This Court founds strength in forming the aforesaid opinion as it is explicit from the defendants evidence before this Court that they were not having any honest belief at the time of filing of criminal complaint, that the accusation made by them against the plaintiffs for the offence of cheating was true as in her evidence affidavit Ex.DW-1/X, it is the stand-alone defence of the defendants that the criminal case was filed against the plaintiffs as they did not handover the original chain of documents pertaining to the plot in question.
So, in the opinion of this Court, the pre-condition of malice also stands satisfied.

Besides the aforesaid discussion, in Radhey Mohan Singh Vs. Kaushalaya Devi, AIR 2003 Delhi 413 (DB), it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that where the finding of the Courts of fact is that the accusation against the plaintiffs made by the defendant was false to his knowledge and that there was enmity between the parties, the conclusion would follow that the prosecution of the plaintiffs was malicious as well as without any reasonable and probable cause.

Dilip Kumar Ray, AIR 2007 SC 976, it was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that malicious prosecution means that the proceedings which are complained of were initiated from a malicious spirit i.e. from an indirect and improper motive and not in furtherance of justice.

entities.text: West Bengal State Electricity Board Vs. Dilip Kumar Ray, AIR 2007 SC 976
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the criminal law was set into motion by lodging the criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 at the instance of the defendants owing to non- handing over the chain of original property documents of the plot in question by the plaintiffs and not due to any kind of cheating, as admitted by the defendants in their written statement as well as the evidence affidavit Ex.PW- 1/X.

The said fact reflects that the criminal complaint of defendants was not genuine and not filed in the furtherance of justice but for the improper motive of exerting pressure upon the plaintiffs for handing over the property documents to the defendants as they were facing problems in handling the property in question.
13.19.So far as the sufficiency of material required for proving the case of the plaintiffs is concerned

,
it is a settled principle of law that while enquiring into whether a fact is true, the sufficiency of evidence is to be seen in the context of standard proof which in civil cases is by preponderance of probability.
Reference can be made to judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in Government of Goa through the Chief Secretary Vs. Maria Julieta D'souza, Civil Appeal No.722/2016.

sentences.text: 13.20.In the light of the admitted facts mentioned hereinabove, aforesaid position of law and discussion of the evidence, this Court is of the opinion that on the scale of preponderance of probability, the plaintiffs are successful in establishing that the defendants launched a malicious prosecution against them and caused them mental and physical harassment and now, liable to compensate them by paying the damages.
14. QUANTUM OF DAMAGES 14.1.

It is a matter of record that during the trial of the present case,
the plaintiffs have not brought on record any document which could quantify the damages sought by them from the defendants.

However, it is also the matter of record that the plaintiffs who are the reputed members of the Society suffered a lot due to the false case filed by the defendants and had to obtain anticipatory bail from the Ld. Sessions Court and also had to represent themselves through counsels at the stage of charge framing.
So, this Court is of the opinion that Rs.10,00,000/- sought by the plaintiffs from the defendants are not on the higher side and a reasonable amount to compensate their losses.
14.2. Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants.
15. ISSUE NO.2:-
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to interest, if so, to what amount and for what period?
The onus to prove this issue is upon the plaintiffs.

Keeping in view the mandate of Section 34 CPC, the plaintiffs are entitled to interest @ 6% per annum i.e. pendete lite and future interest till the date of its realisation.
15.2. Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants.
16.RELIEF 16.1.

Accordingly, in view of the aforesaid discussion and findings on the issues, the plaintiffs are entitled for a decree of Rs.10,00,000/- as damages alongwith interest @ 6% per annum i.e. pendete lite and future interest till the date of its realisation.
Both the defendants are jointly and severely liable to pay the aforesaid amount to the plaintiffs.
Parties are left to bear their own costs.

Dharamsheela Devi examined herself as a defence witness and deposed that she filed the criminal complaint against the plaintiffs as the entire original chain of property documents pertaining to the plot admeasuring 42 sq.yds were not handed over to them by the plaintiffs and due to which they had to face several difficulties and the criminal complaint was not filed with any malice or ulterior motive.
13.6. During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for plaintiffs pleaded that the defendants are liable to pay the damages as the criminal proceedings initiated at their instance ultimately terminated in favour of plaintiffs.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
So, a plaint in a suit for compensation for malicious prosecution merely stating that the plaintiff was prosecuted by or at the instance of the defendant and later on acquitted, would not constitute the valid cause of action.
The present suit has been filed seeking damages for malicious prosecution by the plaintiffs against the defendants for filing a criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 on the basis of which the FIR Ex.PW-1/3 was got lodged and the criminal investigation was initiated which ultimately culminated in filing the chargesheet before the Court against the plaintiffs.
So, the pre-condition of the initiation of a law suit stands satisfied.
b. Favourable termination of law suit.
The criminal prosecution against the plaintiffs which was initiated after the lodging of FIR Ex.PW-1/3 at the instance of defendants stood terminated after the passing of the discharge order Ex.PW-1/6 dated 04.09.2019 passed by Ld.Metropolitan Magistrate at the stage of charge framing.
From the perusal of criminal complaint Ex.PW-1/2 filed on behalf of the defendants on the basis of which the FIR Ex.PW-1/3 was registered, it is crystal clear that the same was filed by taking the plea that the defendants have been cheated by the plaintiffs by transferring a piece of land which did not belong to them.
So, the pre-condition of lack of probable cause also stands satisfied.
However, this Court is of the opinion that even in the absence of any such elaboration if the element of malice is founded on the part of the defendants, from the appreciation of the evidence of the present case, the pre- condition of presence of malice for the prosecution of defendants for the tort of malicious prosecution would be satisfied.
Suresh Kumar And Anr vs Nageshwar Rai And Anr on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57716398/
7 13.15.In
Gangadhar Padhy Vs. Prem Singh, (2014) 211 DLT 104, it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that a prosecution can be held to be malicious only if it is found to be vindictive, initiated to malign the plaintiff before the public or guided by purely personal consideration.
Malicious prosecution is the institution of a criminal or civil proceedings for an improper purpose and without probable cause.
The said fact reflects that the criminal complaint of defendants was not genuine and not filed in the furtherance of justice but for the improper motive of exerting pressure upon the plaintiffs for handing over the property documents to the defendants as they were facing problems in handling the property in question.

,
it is a settled principle of law that while enquiring into whether a fact is true, the sufficiency of evidence is to be seen in the context of standard proof which in civil cases is by preponderance of probability.
It is a matter of record that during the trial of the present case,
the plaintiffs have not brought on record any document which could quantify the damages sought by them from the defendants.
